metric.definition: Market rate per kilowatt per month for leased capacity, the price signal for scarcity in each metro.

reading.body:
Colocation rental rates measure the market rate per kilowatt per month for leased capacity, described as the price signal for scarcity in each metro.

Rates rising after a decade of decline is named as the clearest market evidence that demand has outrun supply, which makes this metric a market-based confirmation of the physical capacity constraints described elsewhere in this collection, interconnection queues and construction lead times, rather than a separate story. The site again draws a line between tracking and republishing, rate data is compiled by commercial research firms listed in a directory, not reproduced directly here.

Its siblings, hyperscaler and colocation capital expenditure and critical equipment lead times, are grouped under Financials and supply chain, together tracing the same capacity crunch through pricing, spending, and physical delivery times.
